# b300 decode latency: PR arms, knobs and a phase timeline (2026-10-16/17)

2 x p6-b300.48xlarge (ap-south-2a), 2 nodes / 16 ranks, GIN type 5, `ovlp=0`,
`--test-first-only` (FP8 dispatch), DeepSeek-V3 shape (7168 / 256 experts / top-8).
Base: `amazon-contributing/DeepEP` main `c105b59`. Arms are merges of a PR head onto it
(`Dockerfile.stack`): `pr89` = #8+#9 (`3c737dc`), `pr16` = `8d45880`, `pr17` = `bb78750`.

**All numbers are in `tables.txt`, generated by `./make_tables.sh` from `logs/` and
`timeline/logs/`.** Section letters below refer to it.

## Findings

1. **Arms (A).** At 128 tok only #8+#9 moves decode (dispatch and reduced combine each
   about -6%). #16 and #17 are flat. At 8192 tok #16 makes combine +14.6%, which
   reproduces the 10-08 result on the newer main.
2. **Floor (B, C).** Dispatch is almost all fixed cost: 1 tok is about 84% of 128 tok.
   1 node (NVLink only) dispatches 128 tok in about 26 us, so going cross-node adds
   about 100 us. Only about 20 us of that is two EFA one-way trips (fi_pingpong one-way
   about 10 us).
3. **SM / channel geometry (D, E).** Dispatch prefers fewer channels and combine prefers
   more. combine inherits its channel count from the dispatch handle, so the two cannot
   be set separately. Best zero-code point: **#8+#9 at 8 SM** (D). #8+#9 at 12 SM with
   `EP_MAX_CHANNELS_PER_SM=3` (E) is equivalent: total channels about 36-40 either way.
   Default #8+#9 runs 5 channels/SM (60 at 12 SM; main 4 = 48).
4. **Timeline (I).** Each kernel's start rail barrier costs 21-28 us. In dispatch, the
   wait from the last RDMA put to the last remote arrival grows with channel count
   (message rate, not latency). In combine, the scale-up NVLink phase dominates, and its
   length is inversely proportional to channel count.
5. **combine batch size (F).** No effect at 12 to 4: a decode channel never fills a
   batch. At 3 or below it is slower. At 8192 tok, batch 4 makes combine +13%.
   **Rejected.**
6. **Scale-up double buffering (J, DB).** Byte-identical timing. The JIT cache key
   confirms the flag was compiled in. **Rejected:** the store is not the bottleneck.
7. **Per-token scale-up cost (J).** In reduced combine each scale-up warp handles about
   19.5 tokens at about 2.5 us each, and the local top-k reduce is 1.3 us of that. At
   hidden 7168 the reduce makes 7 serial load rounds (unroll capped at 4).
   **`EP_COMBINE_REDUCE_UNROLL=7` (G): reduced combine -2.7%.** At 14 it is slower
   overall (register pressure).
8. **Copy epilogue (H, K).** The real copy work is 3-3.5 us in every config. The
   kineto spread of 4-19 us is launch and wait time around the dispatch tail. Part of
   it overlaps dispatch, so summing kernel times over-counts end-to-end latency. In K,
   the "GridDepSync done" and "span" rows are contaminated: a PDL'd next call can start
   before the previous call retires, so those two rows mix two calls. Use only the
   "entry" and "work" rows.

## Experiment layers (none is a proposed upstream patch as-is)

| dir | env knob | what |
|---|---|---|
| `Dockerfile.chcap` | `EP_MAX_CHANNELS_PER_SM` | cap channels/SM in the dispatch channel decision |
| `combine_batch/` | `EP_COMBINE_BATCH_SIZE` | combine tokens per RDMA put (default 12) |
| `scaleup_db/` | `EP_COMBINE_SCALEUP_DB` | double-buffer the combine scale-up warps |
| `reduce_unroll/` | `EP_COMBINE_REDUCE_UNROLL` | unroll cap of the scale-up local reduce (default 4) |
| `timeline/` | (always on in those images) | `%globaltimer` / `clock64` phase stamps, printed by the next call |

Every JIT-visible knob goes through `csrc/jit/compiler.hpp` as a `-D` flag, so it is part
of the JIT cache key. Direct mode (`--allow-hybrid-mode=0`) fails on this stack:
`GIN: DevComm setup failed on all available backends`.
